title: Request Flows and Vendor Management Blueprint
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This blueprint codifies company-wide procedural flows for three common cross-functional operations: access & permissions changes, procurement and expenses, and vendor onboarding (including travel-related approvals). It is intended to be a single reference for requestors, approvers, and operational teams. It emphasizes principles of least privilege, auditability, separation of duties, and risk-proportionate review.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and short-term vendors.
- Covers: Okta/SSO group membership requests, privileged (sudo/K8s/DB) access, change management for production services, purchase requests, vendor onboarding/security review, corporate travel approvals and expense reimbursement.
- Excludes: HR-only processes (benefits, payroll) and customer data access requests governed by contract addenda (see related_pages).

Principles and SLAs:
- Least privilege: grant the minimum role required and set explicit time-to-live when feasible.
- Two-approver model for privileged changes: manager + owning service/product/security reviewer.
- Auditability: all requests must create a tracked ticket (Jira or Procurement Portal) with clear justification and link to approvals.
- SLAs:
  - Standard access requests: respond within 3 business days.
  - Escalation for critical access: initial response within 4 hours, resolution or temporary mitigation within 24 hours.
  - Procurement approval (<= $5k): 5 business days. $5k–$50k: 10 business days. > $50k: 20 business days + procurement committee cadence.

Roles & Ownership:
- Requestor: initiates the ticket with justification, cost center, and expected TTL for access.
- Manager: verifies business need and cost center.
- Security Team: reviews privileged access and vendor security posture.
- Procurement (Finance) Team: executes purchase, contract review, and vendor payments.
- IT/Platform: enacts access changes and monitors expirations.
- Legal: reviews contracts for enterprise vendors or data sharing agreements.

1) Access & Permissions Request Flow (Okta / Internal RBAC)
A. Request submission (Jira access-request template or via Self-Service Portal):
  - Required fields: requestor, manager, justification, resource (service name e.g., inference-runtime-prod), role (e.g., read-only, deploy, db-admin), TTL (if temporary), business owner, risk classification.
  - Attachments: training completion proof (if required), signed NDA for external contractors.
B. Automated validations:
  - Portal checks: ensure requestor is manager-approved in HR system and cost center present.
  - TTL enforcement: default TTL for elevated roles = 7 days unless longer period justified.
C. Approval chain:
  1. Manager approval (manager of requestor).
  2. Service/Product owner approval (if different).
  3. Security review for roles with sensitive scope (e.g., DB admin, SSH, K8s cluster-admin).
D. Implementation & Audit:
  - IT/Platform applies changes via IaC or identity provider automation (Okta group provisioning).
  - Ticket must include implementation record and link to user provisioning audit log.
  - Automated reminders sent 3 days before TTL expiration.
E. Emergency access (break-glass):
  - One-time emergency elevation can be granted with after-action review within 48 hours. Emergency title must include "EMERGENCY" and be tagged for security postmortem.

2) Change Management for Production Services
- Change window: routine non-disruptive changes occur Mon–Fri 03:00–06:00 UTC when possible; disruptive changes require scheduled maintenance with 72h customer/internal notice.
- Risk classification:
  - Low: config tweaks with <1% user impact forecast.
  - Medium: rolling deploys that touch stateful services.
  - High: schema migrations, cross-region DNS changes, or leader election changes.
- Approval & testing:
  1. Dev team runbook + preflight checklist (unit + canary + e2e where applicable).
  2. SRE review for medium/high risk.
  3. Change scheduled in the calendar and communicated to #sre-oncall, #product-updates.
- Rollback: every high/medium change must include a tested rollback plan and a verification checklist for post-rollout validation (latency, error rate, key traces).

3) Procurement & Expenses (high-level rules)
- Thresholds and approvals:
  - <= $5,000: Requestor -> Manager -> Procurement auto-approve.
  - $5,001–$50,000: Requestor -> Manager -> Procurement (finance review) -> Contract owner if recurring.
  - > $50,000: All above + Procurement Committee review + Legal sign-off.
- Purchase types and templates:
  - One-time purchases: use the Procurement Portal form; attach quote and cost center.
  - SaaS subscriptions: require security self-attestation (see vendor onboarding) and renewal cadence.
  - Capital requests: submit CAPEX form (Finance) and include depreciation schedule.
- Payment terms and invoices:
  - Standard net-30 unless negotiated. All invoices routed to AP via procurement ticket with PO number.
- Expense reimbursement:
  - Submit receipts in Expensify within 30 days. Missing receipts require manager exception.
  - Per diem and mileage: follow company scale. Current mileage rate: 0.655 USD/mile.

Quick reference table:
| Spend band | Approval chain | Typical SLA | Docs needed |
|-----------:|----------------|------------:|------------|
| <= $5k | Manager -> Procurement | 5 business days | Quote/receipt, cost center |
| $5k–$50k | Manager -> Procurement -> Finance | 10 business days | Vendor security attestation, quote |
| > $50k | Committee + Legal | 20 business days | Contract, SOC2 or equivalent, legal redlines |

4) Vendor Onboarding & Security Checklist
- Tiering by data exposure:
  - Tier A (restricted): vendors that handle customer PII, model weights, or infra with access to production systems. Require SOC2 Type II, penetration test report, contract MR, and use of customer-approved key management (KMS/HSM) if handling secrets.
  - Tier B (internal-confidential): vendors that process internal analytics, require security questionnaire and encryption-in-transit.
  - Tier C (public): marketing, event vendors; basic company insurance & tax form.
- Onboarding steps (checklist):
  1. Business sponsor opens vendor request in Procurement Portal with SOW/quote.
  2. Procurement triage: confirm spend band and request security tier.
  3. Security team performs questionnaire and provides required controls (SLA, encryption, incident response).
  4. Legal reviews & signs contract; include data processing addendum if Tier A/B.
  5. IT/Platform configures network & access (VPC peering, firewall rules) where necessary.
  6. Finance sets up payment terms and cost center mapping.
- Required minimums for Tier A:
| Requirement | Expectation |
|-------------|-------------|
| SOC2 Type II | Report within last 18 months or compensating controls |
| Incident response | 24/7 email + 2 business hour SLA for critical incidents |
| Data handling | Encryption at rest and in transit; data deletion policy defined |

- Deprovisioning: vendor termination checklist includes revoking access, cert/key rotation, verifying data deletion, and final invoice reconciliation.

5) Travel & Expense Policy (operational alignment)
- Approval flow: Requestor -> Manager -> Finance reviewer (if > $2k or > 5 people) -> People Ops (if international visas needed).
- Booking: employees are encouraged to use the corporate travel portal for preferred vendors and negotiated rates. Exceptions require manager + travel admin approval.
- Reimbursement timelines: 30 days submission; reimbursements processed within next payroll cycle.
- Safety & compliance: employees traveling to restricted countries must consult with Security & People Ops 10 business days before travel.

Templates and Forms (links & sample fields)
- Access Request (Jira template): fields={requestor, manager, resource, role, justification, TTL, business owner, CI/CD impact, attachments}.
- Procurement Portal: fields={project, cost-center, frequency, vendor-tier, SOW, quote, security-tier}.
- Vendor Security Questionnaire: standard 40-question form (available as spreadsheet in /confluence/security-and-compliance/).
- Travel Request: fields={purpose, dates, attendees, estimated cost, manager approval}.

Operational automation recommendations:
- Integrate Okta group provisioning with Jira tickets so approvals trigger automated provisioning events.
- Enforce TTLs via automation; expired elevated entitlements send automatic re-review tickets.
- Procurement Portal should emit webhook events to Finance systems (NetSuite) with PO mapping.

Escalation & Exceptions:
- Exceptions must be documented in the ticket and approved by: manager + one delegate from Procurement or Security depending on exception type.
- Critical path escalations: unresolved critical access requests escalate to the SRE Director and CTO oncall after 24 hours.

Metrics to track (owner suggestions):
- Mean time to approve access requests (IT/Platform).
- Percentage of vendor contracts with SOC2 (Procurement).
- Number of emergency access events and time-to-postmortem (Security).
- Procurement cycle time by spend band (Finance).

Appendices:
A. Standard Jira labels and components to apply: labels={access-request, vendor-onboard, procurement, travel}. Components={IT, Finance, Security, Legal}.
B. Example access-request JSON payload (for automation):
{
  "requestor": "alice@redwood.ai",
  "resource": "inference-runtime-prod",
  "role": "deploy",
  "ttl_days": 7
}
C. Contacts:
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.ai (team: Procurement, Slack: #procurement)
- Security intake: security-intake@redwood.ai (Slack: #security-request)
- IT/Platform: platform-ops@redwood.ai (Slack: #platform-requests)
